answer.origin: Primary source: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR, record 'incoming'), filed for an event dated August 17, 2026, with the press release furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The statement is the company's own disclosure, stated as of August 17, 2026.
answer.note: NVIDIA's 8-K says that on August 17, 2026 it entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy, the lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio). An affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC is the tenant and is expected to deploy NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform there. NVIDIA's cumulative payment obligation for the initial commitment is capped at $105 billion. Payments are conditional, including the lessor satisfying ready-for-service conditions, which are expected to begin in 2028. Under a Trigger Event (OpenAI insolvency causing lease default, or OpenAI payment failure), NVIDIA pays generally the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and recoveries from re-leasing or sale. OpenAI agreed to reimburse NVIDIA for amounts actually paid. Each Agreement terminates at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI under its terms, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events. NVIDIA also may provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 GW at its sole discretion. Read conditionally: this is a disclosed, large but capped, contingent credit-support obligation that makes NVIDIA's economics at this site depend substantially on OpenAI's ability to pay and on the lessor delivering the site on schedule. It supports the view that NVIDIA is actively underwriting AI data center capacity for a specific tenant and platform, which is evidence about NVIDIA's own demand-side commitments and the scale of its exposure, not a reported result or a confirmed order flow from OpenAI.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not in the record; the 8-K says it will be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026. Guaranteed minimum values, lease-by-lease caps, and the mechanics for the $105 billion cap are therefore unknown.

The 8-K does not disclose the probability of a Trigger Event, NVIDIA's expected payout, or any accounting treatment or recorded liability for the guaranties, so the expected financial effect cannot be estimated from this source.
The 8-K gives no lease commencement dates beyond 'expected beginning in 2028'. The timing of the ready-for-service conditions and of any payment exposure is therefore uncertain.
The conditions and status of the additional 3.8 GW credit support are not described beyond NVIDIA's sole discretion. Whether any such support has been provided is unknown.

The source does not disclose OpenAI's credit profile, the terms of its lease payments, or the amount of any reimbursement actually made, so the strength of the OpenAI reimbursement backstop is unknown.
The press release (Exhibit 99.1) is referenced but its contents are not in the supplied record beyond the 8-K's summary.

Forward-looking statements in the 8-K are subject to the stated safe-harbor risk factors; the source gives no independent confirmation of the Portsmouth Site's development progress, power, or land status.
follow_up: Retrieve the full Agreements when filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, and check guaranteed minimum values, the $105 billion cap mechanics, termination events, and ready-for-service conditions.
Check NVIDIA's subsequent 10-Q and 10-K for recognized liabilities, fair value of the guaranties, and disclosed contingent exposure tied to the Portsmouth Site.
Check the Exhibit 99.1 press release and any OpenAI announcement for lease commencement timing, tenant commitments, and the status of the additional 3.8 GW.
Check the SB Energy and lessor disclosures or filings for the Portsmouth Site's construction and power milestones relative to the 2028 expectation.
Track any Trigger Event disclosures or reports of OpenAI payment or insolvency issues affecting the leases.
